title: PLAYER 2 HEARS HOW THE CONVOY AND THE RAMPAGE END
why: When a machine convoy or an Overseer rampage ended, only the host window said it: CONVOY DOWN / SEARCH THE CRATE when the carrier was killed, CONVOY AWAY when it got away at its destination, CONVOY ARRIVED / THEY STAY when it reached its destination in view and stayed, and OVERSEER RETURNS when the rampage ran out with the Overseer alive. Player 2 window runs none of the event code that says those lines; it already says the warning and the start of each event, not the end. Proven in a staged pair in one window: each of those endings had the host say its line and player 2 window say nothing. The host now remembers which end line it said at the moment it said it and sends that in the world word, and player 2 window says the same line, once, when the event goes from live to over. Because it is the line the host said, not a guess from the state half a second later, a carrier that stayed and then died, or an Overseer that went home and then died, before the next word still gives player 2 the same line as the host. A convoy that times out and an Overseer that is killed still say nothing on either window. Say only: the crate, the bodies and the boss are still the host's.
now: In co-op, both players now hear when the convoy is down, gets away or arrives and stays, and when the Overseer returns to his lair.
